REGIONS.name: Cranbia
REGIONS.blurb: Industrial, urban and educated. Home to the capital, Cranebo.

REGIONS.name: Yamlin
REGIONS.blurb: The trade gateway to the wider world. Progressives, immigrants and fed-up nationalists live side by side; the rich profit from trade and cheap labour while others feel left behind.

REGIONS.name: Erland
REGIONS.blurb: The nationalist heartland and breadbasket of Cranebonistan.

REGIONS.name: Alinni
REGIONS.blurb: Conquered from the Southern Trueants fifty years ago. The Alinnian minority has never fully settled into Cranebonistan, and tensions run high.

REGIONS.name: Fauran
REGIONS.blurb: Sparse, nomadic and the poorest region, with a disputed border with Dillihan.

name: Southern
Trueants
FOREIGN.blurb: Corrupt and in economic crisis. Its leader still claims Alinni.
FOREIGN.summary: Cranebonistan took Alinni from the Southern Trueants in a war fifty years ago, and the Trueants have never accepted it. The country is corrupt and stuck in a long economic crisis, and its president keeps his supporters loyal by promising that Alinni will one day come home.
facts: Sells Cranebonistan a third of its gas

name: Dillihan
Republic
FOREIGN.blurb: The regional powerhouse. Disputes the Fauran border.
FOREIGN.summary: The richest and strongest country in the region, economically and militarily. Dillihan disputes parts of the Fauran border, and its patrols regularly cross into land Cranebonian herders consider theirs. It would like a pipeline across Fauran to the sea.
facts: Strongest economy and army in the region

name: Bordon
Federation
FOREIGN.blurb: A fragile federation held together by a charismatic generalissimo.
FOREIGN.summary: A union of several nations that would probably fall apart without the generalissimo at its head. His health is the subject of constant rumours. Erland's border towns watch nervously: if the federation breaks up, refugees and trouble will come north.

name: James
FOREIGN.blurb: Refuses to join Bordon and trusts Cranebonistan to protect it. Rich in rare materials.
FOREIGN.summary: A small country with very large reserves of rare materials. James refuses to join the Bordon Federation and relies on Cranebonistan to defend it. In return, Cranebonian companies hold favourable mining deals there, which Potania would love to take over.

PARTIES.name: National Unity Party
PARTIES.blurb: The ruling party. Nationalist, traditional, strongest in Erland.

PARTIES.name: Cranebonian Labour Front
PARTIES.blurb: The old left. Unions, factories, public services.

PARTIES.name: Open Cranebonistan
PARTIES.blurb: Liberal and pro-business. Popular with Yamlin's traders and the urban rich.

PARTIES.name: Alinni People's Voice
PARTIES.blurb: Speaks for the Alinnian minority. Wants autonomy and peace.

PARTY_TEMPLATES.name: People's Awakening
PARTY_TEMPLATES.pitch: Bread, wages and dignity. Take on the factory owners and the comfortable politicians who protect them.
PARTY_TEMPLATES.targets: Working class, young voters, Cranbia and Fauran

PARTY_TEMPLATES.name: Homeland First
PARTY_TEMPLATES.pitch: Close the borders, stand up to the Trueants and Dillihan, and give the country back to ordinary Cranebonians.
PARTY_TEMPLATES.targets: Erland, older voters, fed-up nationalists in Yamlin

PARTY_TEMPLATES.name: New Horizon
PARTY_TEMPLATES.pitch: Competent, modern and above the old quarrels. Sell yourself as the adults the country never had.
PARTY_TEMPLATES.targets: Middle class, educated Cranbia, young professionals

PARTY_TEMPLATES.name: Land and Hearth
PARTY_TEMPLATES.pitch: The capital has forgotten the villages. Farmers, herders and small towns deserve their fair share.
PARTY_TEMPLATES.targets: Erland and Fauran, rural working class

PARTY_TEMPLATES.name: Enough!
PARTY_TEMPLATES.pitch: They are all the same. Burn the old system down and let the people decide directly.
PARTY_TEMPLATES.targets: Anyone fed up with politics: the young, Fauran, Alinni

PARTY_TEMPLATES.pitch: Start from a blank manifesto and decide everything yourself.

EVENTS.title: The Pezo slides against the Golban dollar
EVENTS.text: The Cranebonian Pezo has lost 14% against the Golban dollar in a month. Bread prices in Cranebo are climbing, importers in Yamlin are panicking, and every talk show wants a party leader on the line tonight.

choices.label: Argue for tariffs on Golban imports

lines.text: Cranebonistan should not be paying Golba's bills. Targeted tariffs will protect our producers while the Pezo recovers.
Every Golban gadget in our shops is a Cranebonian job shipped abroad. Tax them until it hurts!
My grandmother never bought a Golban tomato in her life, and she lived to ninety-four.

choices.label: Demand high interest rates to stop the bleeding

lines.text: Painful medicine is still medicine. Raise the rates now, or pay twice as much next year.
The Central Bank is asleep at the wheel. Raise the rates, or resign!
If your mortgage goes up, thank the clowns who let the Pezo rot.

choices.label: Blame the Alinnian minority for being lazy

lines.text: While honest Cranebonians work, some people in Alinni live on our taxes and hate us for it.
We all know which region takes more than it gives. I don't need to say the name.
The Alinnians want a Trueant passport and a Cranebonian pension. Pick one!

choices.label: Call it a temporary slide that will pass soon

lines.text: Currencies rise and fall. Our economy is stronger than one bad month.
Relax. The Pezo has seen worse, and so have we.
Only cowards and Golban bankers panic over one bad month.

government.text: The NUP finance minister says the Pezo is "fundamentally strong" and announces no measures.

EVENTS.title: The minimum wage debate
EVENTS.text: The Assembly is voting on raising the minimum wage by 20%. Unions say families cannot afford rent. Small business owners say they will have to fire people.

choices.label: Back the full 20% rise
Propose a smaller rise with tax relief for small firms
Oppose it. Jobs first

EVENTS.title: Rents in Cranebo double in three years
EVENTS.text: A new report shows the average rent in the capital now eats 60% of a young worker's salary. Landlords blame the shortage of new buildings.

choices.label: Promise a rent cap

lines.text: The landlords have had their party. Now it's the tenants' turn.
A temporary cap will give families breathing room while we build.
Sixty percent of your salary for one room and a view of the bins? No.

choices.label: Promise a huge public housing programme

lines.text: The state built Cranebo once. It can build it again.
Cranes on the skyline, keys in young people's hands.
A hundred thousand homes, and not one of them for a speculator!

choices.label: Call for cutting red tape so developers can build

lines.text: We have a shortage because we forbid building. Let people build.
If it takes four years to get a permit for a shed, imagine a tower block.
Tenants complain about rents, then fight every new building on their street.

choices.label: Say immigrants are driving up rents

lines.text: Every new arrival is another name on the waiting list ahead of yours.
Ten Norbanians to a flat and the rent still goes up. Explain that.
Rapid migration has put pressure on housing. We must plan for it honestly.

EVENTS.title: Government plans to raise the retirement age
EVENTS.text: The National Unity government wants to raise the retirement age from 62 to 66 to save the pension fund. Retirees are furious; economists mostly agree it is needed.

choices.label: Fight it in the streets
Support it as the responsible choice
Say the young should pay more instead

EVENTS.title: Viral video: graduates driving taxis
EVENTS.text: A video of three engineering graduates driving taxis in Cranebo has been watched nine million times. Youth unemployment has reached 24%, and the comments are furious.

choices.label: Promise a state job guarantee for under-30s

lines.text: A degree should lead to a job. Under us, every graduate under thirty will be offered one.
We are wasting a whole generation, and the government is filming it!
Nobody should need an engineering degree to know the way to the airport.

choices.label: Call for tax cuts for start-ups

lines.text: Tomorrow's jobs come from new companies. Let them keep more of what they earn.
Let these engineers build something. Worst case, they're back in the taxi.
Stop crying on the internet and start a company.

choices.label: Launch a meme campaign about it

lines.text: We made a video too. It's shorter, and the taxi has a better driver.
Rate my rivals' cabinet: three taxi drivers and a minister who's never had a job.
We will put the facts where young people actually look. Short, clear and true.

choices.label: Blame the older generation

lines.text: They bought houses for a song, then pulled the ladder up behind them.
OK, grandpa. Your pension is my rent.
I love my parents. I just wish they'd left us a little of the country.

EVENTS.title: Robots replace dock workers in Yamlin
EVENTS.text: The Port of Yamlin will automate its container terminal, cutting 6,000 jobs. The owners promise lower prices for everyone.

choices.label: Demand a ban on port automation
Promise retraining for every laid-off worker
Welcome it: progress can't be stopped
Blame Norbanian workers for the cheap labour race

EVENTS.title: Golba offers a free trade agreement
EVENTS.text: The United Federation of Golba, Cranebonistan's biggest trading partner, has offered to scrap tariffs on both sides. Yamlin's port authority is thrilled. Erland's farmers are not.

choices.label: Urge the government to sign the deal
Demand it be rejected to protect Erland's farmers
Back it only with strong worker protections
Call it Golban economic colonialism

government.text: The government says it is "carefully studying" Golba's offer.

EVENTS.title: Refugee ships dock in Yamlin
EVENTS.text: Three overcrowded ships from war-torn Norbanistan arrived overnight. Two thousand people are waiting on the quay. Dock workers are blocking the gates, and the shipping companies want them let in.

choices.label: Welcome them and demand a fair asylum process

lines.text: These are families fleeing a war. We will hear every claim fairly and quickly.
Shame on anyone who would leave children on a quay. Open the gates!
My great-grandfather came off a boat with one suitcase. Look how that turned out.

choices.label: Demand the ports be closed: Cranebonistan is full

lines.text: Compassion has limits, and so does Yamlin. The ports must close until there is a plan.
Not one more ship! Cranebonistan is not the world's waiting room!
Send them to Golba. Golba loves lecturing us about human rights.

choices.label: Say Yamlin's businesses need the workers

lines.text: Yamlin's port runs on labour we no longer have. Managed arrivals are good economics.
Somebody has to pick the fruit, and it isn't going to be the minister.
If your job can be done by a man off a boat, maybe ask yourself why.

choices.label: Demand that Golba and Potania share the burden

lines.text: This is an international crisis and it needs an international answer. Golba and Potania must share the load.
We'll do our bit. But Golba has a lot more spare rooms than we do.
Golba armed every side in Norbanistan's war. Let Golba take the ships!

government.text: The government lets the ships dock but holds everyone in a closed camp on the quay.

EVENTS.title: Alinnian-language schools bill
EVENTS.text: A bill would let schools in Alinni teach in the Alinnian language. Alinnian parents have campaigned for it for decades. Nationalists call it the first step to separation.

choices.label: Support the bill
Propose optional Alinnian lessons instead
Say one country needs one language

EVENTS.title: Civil partnership bill
EVENTS.text: Open Cranebonistan has proposed legal civil partnerships for same-sex couples. Polls are split almost exactly down the middle, by age.

choices.label: Champion the bill
Call it a matter of conscience and give your MPs a free vote
Oppose it to protect the traditional family

EVENTS.title: Make Harvest Day a national holiday?
EVENTS.text: Erland's ancient Harvest Day festival is hugely popular, and a petition to make it a national holiday has a million signatures. Business groups grumble about lost working days.

choices.label: Back the petition and dance at the festival
Propose a 'Festival of All Peoples' including Alinnian traditions
Say the country can't afford another holiday

EVENTS.title: Robberies surge in Cranebo
EVENTS.text: A string of violent robberies in the capital's suburbs has dominated the news for a week. The police say they lack officers; residents say they no longer feel safe at night.

choices.label: Demand 10,000 more police officers

lines.text: Safety is the first freedom. We will put ten thousand more officers on the streets.
Criminals should fear the night, not the families of Cranebo!
My mother won't take the bus after dark any more. That's not a capital, that's a hostage situation.

choices.label: Blame poverty and promise youth centres

lines.text: Prison is the most expensive way to fail a young man. Give them somewhere to go.
Every kid with a football pitch is a kid without a knife.
If you want fewer robbers, stop running the country like one.

choices.label: Blame Norbanian gangs

lines.text: These gangs came on the boats, and they can leave on them.
Funny how the robberies started when the ships arrived.
Organised gangs with foreign links must be broken up and their members deported.

choices.label: Walk the streets with residents at night

lines.text: I'll walk these streets myself tonight. Who's coming?
I've come to listen, not to make promises.
If the government won't patrol these streets, the people will.

government.text: The Interior Minister blames the previous government and promises "a review".

EVENTS.title: Trueant president: "Alinni will come home"
EVENTS.text: At a rally broadcast across the border, the president of the Southern Trueants promised that Alinni will return to the Trueant nation "within this generation". Alinnian community leaders have asked everyone to stay calm.

choices.label: Demand troops on the Trueant border

lines.text: Alinni is Cranebonian, and that border must be defended with more than words.
Let him come and try. Our soldiers will be waiting.
The Trueants can't keep their own lights on. Let them come; we'll leave ours on for them.

choices.label: Call for calm talks with the Trueants

lines.text: Rhetoric is cheap and war is not. We should talk, and keep talking.
Two old neighbours shouting over a fence. Somebody has to put the kettle on.
I will not let warmongers in either capital turn our children into soldiers!

choices.label: Promise a development fund for Alinni

lines.text: The best answer to the Trueants is an Alinni where people want to stay.
Build the roads, open the schools, and nobody in Alinni will want to go anywhere.
Cranebo has ignored Alinni for fifty years. No wonder the vultures are circling!

choices.label: Mock the Trueant economy on live TV

lines.text: A man who can't pay his own teachers wants another region? Good luck to him.
The Southern Trueants: the only country where the power goes off more often than the president.
Their president is a thief with a microphone, and everyone in his country knows it.

government.text: The Foreign Ministry summons the Trueant ambassador for a formal protest.

country.note: Its president promised that Alinni "will come home" within a generation.

EVENTS.title: Dillihan patrol enters Fauran pastures
EVENTS.text: A Dillihan border patrol crossed into grazing land claimed by Fauran herders and confiscated forty camels. The government has issued a "strongly worded note". Herders say nobody in Cranebo cares about them.

choices.label: Demand a firm military response
Propose a joint grazing agreement
Blame the weak government in Cranebo
Stay quiet

government.text: The government sends Dillihan a "strongly worded note".

country.note: Its border patrols seized forty camels from Fauran herders.

EVENTS.title: Potania wants more of James's rare earths
EVENTS.text: Potania, the biggest buyer of rare materials from James, is pressuring the little country to sell mining rights directly instead of through Cranebonian companies. James has quietly asked Cranebo for support.

choices.label: Promise to defend James's sovereignty
Say the mining companies should cut their own deal with Potania
Call for nationalising Cranebonian mining stakes
Say this is a matter for James and Potania

country.note: Potania is pressing it for direct rights to its rare-earth mines.

EVENTS.title: Bordon's generalissimo collapses at a parade
EVENTS.text: The generalissimo who holds the Bordon Federation together collapsed during a military parade. State TV insists he is fine. Border towns in Erland are worried about what happens if the federation breaks apart.

choices.label: Call for the southern border to be sealed
Urge the government to offer itself as a mediator
Hint that Cranebonistan could gain land if it falls
Wish him a speedy recovery

country.note: The generalissimo collapsed at a military parade. Rumours about his health are everywhere.

EVENTS.title: Golba asks for sanctions on the Southern Trueants
EVENTS.text: Golba wants its partners to stop buying Trueant grain and gas over the Trueants' corruption and border threats. Cranebonistan buys a third of its gas from them.

choices.label: Urge the government to join the sanctions
Say Cranebonistan must refuse: we are nobody's servant
Back sanctions only if Golba pays for the higher gas bills

country.note: Golba is pushing its partners to sanction it.

EVENTS.title: Dillihan proposes a gas pipeline through Fauran
EVENTS.text: Dillihan wants to build a pipeline across Fauran to the port of Yamlin. It would bring jobs and transit fees, but herders say it will cut their ancient migration routes.

choices.label: Back the pipeline
Back it only if the state owns half
Not one metre of Fauran soil for Dillihan

country.note: Proposed a gas pipeline across Fauran to the port of Yamlin.

EVENTS.title: James asks for a Cranebonian military base
EVENTS.text: Worried by Bordon and Potania, the government of James has asked Cranebonistan to station troops in the country. The base would protect the mines and cost a fortune.

choices.label: Urge the government to send troops
Propose training and equipment instead
Say our soldiers are not mine guards for corporations

country.note: Asked Cranebonistan to station troops on its soil.

EVENTS.title: Floods devastate Yamlin's old town
EVENTS.text: Three days of storms have flooded Yamlin's old town. Thousands have lost their homes. The prime minister is on holiday and has not commented yet.

choices.label: Go there today and fill sandbags with volunteers

lines.text: Hand me a shovel.
Today is not for politics. Today is for Yamlin.
I'm here. Where is the prime minister?

choices.label: Attack the prime minister for being on holiday

lines.text: Yamlin is drowning and the prime minister is sunbathing!
Somebody send the prime minister a postcard. He seems to like them.
The prime minister should be here. Leadership means showing up.

choices.label: Post a sympathy message from your yacht

lines.text: Thoughts and prayers to Yamlin from the beautiful Potanian coast!
My thoughts are with Yamlin. I am following events closely.
Stay dry, Yamlin! I'm with you in spirit, and in a very small boat.

government.text: The prime minister is on holiday. His office says he is "monitoring the situation".

EVENTS.title: Cranebonistan wins the Continental Cup
EVENTS.text: The national football team has beaten Dillihan 2-1 in the final. A million people are celebrating in the streets of Cranebo tonight.

choices.label: Celebrate with fans in the main square
Say the win proves Cranebonians are superior to Dillihanis
Promise free football pitches in every town

EVENTS.title: Invitation to the big TV debate
EVENTS.text: For the first time, your party has been invited to the national leaders' debate. Seven million people are expected to watch.

choices.label: Prepare for weeks and stay calm
Attack the host as a puppet of the elites
Decline: debates are theatre

EVENTS.title: Earthquake in Fauran
EVENTS.text: A strong earthquake has hit the Fauran steppe. Nomad camps are scattered and roads are cut. Aid is slow to arrive from Cranebo.

choices.label: Organise a party aid convoy
Demand an emergency reconstruction fund
Say nomads should finally settle in proper towns

EVENTS.title: Pop star Lira Vey wants to endorse you
EVENTS.text: The country's biggest pop star, with twelve million followers, has offered to appear at your next rally. She is adored by the young and once called the Harvest Day festival "boring".

choices.label: Accept and share the stage with her
Accept, but keep it low-key
Decline politely

EVENTS.title: Patients die waiting in hospital corridors
EVENTS.text: Leaked figures show 400 patients died last year while waiting for treatment in overcrowded hospitals. Nurses have been working double shifts for months.

choices.label: Promise to hire 20,000 nurses
Call for opening hospitals to private investors
Visit a hospital and thank the nurses

government.text: The Health Minister says waiting times are "a European problem".

EVENTS.title: Smog chokes Cranbia
EVENTS.text: The air in Cranbia's industrial belt was declared hazardous for the tenth day this winter. Doctors want the dirtiest factories closed; the factories employ 80,000 people.

choices.label: Demand the worst factories close now
Propose five years and state money for factories to clean up
Say smog is the price of jobs

EVENTS.title: Mobile schools for Fauran's nomads
EVENTS.text: Only half of Fauran's nomad children go to school. A charity proposes travelling schools that move with the herds.

choices.label: Promise national funding if you win
Demand compulsory schooling, strictly enforced
Say it should be left to the charity

EVENTS.title: Drought hits the Erland harvest
EVENTS.text: Erland's wheat harvest is expected to be the worst in thirty years. Farmers are selling livestock they can no longer feed, and bakeries in Cranebo are warning of higher prices.

choices.label: Demand emergency subsidies for farmers

lines.text: Erland feeds this country. In a bad year, the country must feed Erland.
No farmer should have to sell the cow that feeds his children.
Cranebo spends millions on statues and nothing on the people who grow its bread!

choices.label: Say the market should be left to adjust

lines.text: Subsidies keep weak farms alive and strong ones waiting. Let prices do their work.
Farming is a business. Some businesses fail.
My uncle farmed for forty years without a penny from the state. Never stopped complaining, mind you.

choices.label: Call for cheap grain imports from Bordon

lines.text: Bread prices matter to every family. Bordon grain will keep them down this winter.
A loaf is a loaf. My kids can't tell where the wheat came from.
Erland's farmers have had their hand out for decades. Time for some competition.

choices.label: Pray for rain with farmers at a village shrine

lines.text: I'll stand with these farmers in the sun, and in the rain when it comes.
Faith and hard work have carried Erland through droughts before. They will again.
Some people in the capital laugh at prayer. Let them. Erland knows better.

government.text: The government promises a study on the effects of the drought, due next year.

EVENTS.title: Metalworkers strike in Cranbia
EVENTS.text: Forty thousand metalworkers have walked out across Cranbia's industrial belt over wages eaten by inflation. Factory owners say they cannot pay more without closing plants.

choices.label: Join the picket line

lines.text: Forty thousand people cannot live on promises. Pay them!
I brought tea for the night shift. The owners brought lawyers.
These workers are asking for wages that keep up with prices. That is not radical. It is fair.

choices.label: Side with the factory owners

lines.text: If the factories close, nobody gets a raise. Cranbia needs a settlement that keeps it working.
Strikes are a luxury for people who've never had to make a payroll.
My father ran a workshop with six men. A month like this would have closed him.

choices.label: Call for state arbitration

lines.text: Put both sides in a room with an independent arbitrator, and don't let them out until it's done.
Nobody wins a strike. Get them round a table, and bring biscuits.
The government is hiding under its desk. Arbitration, now!

choices.label: Say the strike is funded by foreign agitators

lines.text: Somebody is paying for these banners, and it isn't the metalworkers.
Ask who funds the strike committee. I hear they speak Dillihani.
The public deserves to know whether foreign money is behind this dispute.

government.text: The government declares the strike illegal and threatens fines.

EVENTS.title: Hot mic: you called Erland farmers "simple"
EVENTS.text: A microphone you thought was off recorded you joking that Erland farmers are "simple people who vote for whoever gives them a tractor". The clip is everywhere.

choices.label: Apologise sincerely and visit Erland
Double down: someone has to say it
Claim the clip is a Dillihani deepfake

EVENTS.title: A tough interview on Channel One
EVENTS.text: A famous interviewer asks you live on air: "Should Alinni have more autonomy, yes or no?" Your advisers are frantically waving at you from behind the camera.

choices.label: "Yes. They deserve to run their own schools and roads."
"Never. Alinni is Cranebonistan, full stop."
Answer both ways in the same sentence

EVENTS.title: Rally crowd demands: "No more taxes!"
EVENTS.text: At a packed rally in Erland, the crowd starts chanting for you to promise no new taxes ever. The cameras are rolling.

choices.label: Promise: "Not one new tax, ever!"
Promise to tax the rich instead
Tell them honestly that schools cost money

EVENTS.title: Your deputy in a nightclub brawl
EVENTS.text: Your party's deputy leader was filmed throwing a chair in a Cranebo nightclub. He says he was defending a friend.

choices.label: Expel him from the party
Defend him: the elites want to bring us down
Say nothing and hope it passes

EVENTS.title: NUP minister caught with a suitcase of cash
EVENTS.text: The Minister of Infrastructure was photographed accepting a suitcase from a construction tycoon. The National Unity Party calls it "a gift between old friends".

choices.label: Lead the charge: "The whole system is rotten!"

lines.text: One suitcase? This whole government is a suitcase!
A gift between old friends? I have old friends too. They give me socks.
This is not one minister's failure. It is a system that rewards it.

choices.label: Demand an independent investigation

lines.text: Let independent investigators follow the money, wherever it leads.
Open the suitcase, count the money, and show us the receipts.
Investigate, prosecute, and let the cameras watch!

choices.label: Stay quiet: you know that tycoon too

lines.text: I won't comment while the matter is under investigation.
No comment. I don't know anything about suitcases. I travel light.
Everyone does it. At least he did it in person.

EVENTS.title: Labour leader's thesis was copied
EVENTS.text: Journalists found that Sanna Brokk, leader of the Labour Front, copied most of her university thesis. Labour voters are embarrassed.

choices.label: Mock her mercilessly on social media
Invite disappointed Labour voters to join you
Say there are more important issues

EVENTS.title: Mass protests in Alinni over your remarks
EVENTS.text: Fifty thousand Alinnians marched through the regional capital, carrying signs with your face crossed out. The Trueant president has praised the protesters.

choices.label: Apologise to the Alinnian community
Say the protests prove the Trueants are behind it
Ignore them

EVENTS.title: Turned-away refugee ship stranded at sea
EVENTS.text: The government gave in to calls like yours and turned the ship away. It has been drifting for three weeks with little food or water. Photographs of children on deck are on every front page.

choices.label: Insist the ship stays out: rules are rules
Demand an exception for the children

EVENTS.title: Experts confirm your "deepfake" clip was real
EVENTS.text: Three independent labs have confirmed the hot mic recording was genuine. The Dillihan embassy is demanding an apology.

choices.label: Admit it and apologise to everyone
Call the labs part of the conspiracy

EVENTS.title: Leak: your party took money from Dillihan
EVENTS.text: Bank records show your party received millions from a Dillihan state company, while Dillihani patrols were seizing herds in Fauran.

choices.label: Deny everything
Return the money and apologise

EVENTS.title: Leak: Trueant money in your party accounts
EVENTS.text: Leaked emails show the Southern Trueant government funded your party, the same government that claims Alinni. Nationalists call it treason.

choices.label: Deny everything
Return the money and apologise

EVENTS.title: Leak: Potanian mining money behind your campaign
EVENTS.text: Journalists traced campaign donations back to a Potanian mining giant that wants James's rare earths. James's ambassador is "deeply disappointed".

choices.label: Deny everything
Return the money and apologise

EVENTS.title: Leak: Golban lobbyists funded your party
EVENTS.text: A Golban trade lobby has been paying for your social media ads. Critics say you are a puppet of Cranebonistan's biggest trading partner.

choices.label: Deny everything
Say Golba is a friend and there's nothing to hide

EVENTS.title: Leak: a tycoon's suitcase in your party office
EVENTS.text: A former staffer says construction tycoon Orvan Sell delivered cash to your party in a suitcase. It looks exactly like the NUP scandal you may have attacked.

choices.label: Deny everything
Return the money and apologise

EVENTS.title: The bank transfers are published
EVENTS.text: Your denial lasted until a newspaper printed the actual bank transfers. Even your own members are asking questions.

choices.label: Fire your party treasurer and apologise
Call it fake news and rally your base

EVENTS.title: Referendum rallies turn violent in Alinni
EVENTS.text: Nationalist counter-protesters attacked a march for your referendum. Forty people are in hospital, and both sides blame you.

choices.label: Blame the nationalist thugs
Condemn violence on both sides
Quietly drop the referendum

EVENTS.title: Police raids empty Yamlin's docks
EVENTS.text: The government copied your idea. After a week of raids, half the dock workers have vanished and ships are waiting to unload.

choices.label: Take the credit: "We said it first"
Ask for mercy for families with children
Attack the government for doing it badly

EVENTS.title: The rich move their money to Golba
EVENTS.text: Bankers report record transfers to Golban accounts since your wealth tax proposal. The Pezo dips again.

choices.label: Call them traitors
Soften it to a smaller tax
Propose a tax on leaving with your money

EVENTS.title: Generals praise you; economists do the maths
EVENTS.text: Retired generals call your defence plan "the first serious idea in years". Economists say it would cost more than every hospital in the country.

choices.label: Say security has no price
Pay for it with a tax on the rich
Quietly halve the figure

EVENTS.title: Trueant TV calls you "our friend in Cranebo"
EVENTS.text: Your secret talks leaked. Trueant state television is praising you, which is the worst thing that could happen to you in Erland.

choices.label: Laugh it off
Loudly condemn the Trueant regime
Defend the talks

country.note: Its state TV praised your secret talks with the Trueant opposition.

EVENTS.title: A minister on your list sues you
EVENTS.text: One of the officials you named is suing you for libel, and his lawyers say your evidence is a newspaper clipping and a rumour.

choices.label: Fight it in court
Apologise and settle
Say the courts are corrupt too

EVENTS.title: Economists: your pension promise would bankrupt the state
EVENTS.text: Every major economist in the country has signed a letter saying your pension promise costs a third of the national budget.

choices.label: Stand by every word
Make it "double by 2040"
Say the economists work for Golban banks

EVENTS.title: Bordon calls your pact "a provocation"
EVENTS.text: The generalissimo's spokesman says any pact with James would be "a hostile act against the Federation".

choices.label: Stand firm
Reassure Bordon
Call the generalissimo a dying tyrant

country.note: Called a Cranebonian defence pact with James "a provocation".

EVENTS.title: Teachers march against your curriculum plans
EVENTS.text: Thirty thousand teachers marched through Cranebo against religion in schools. Several carried your face on a placard.

choices.label: Back down on the schools part
Call the teachers ideologues
Invite them to talks

EVENTS.title: Dillihan: "Those pastures are Dillihani"
EVENTS.text: Dillihan's foreign minister says the herders' land you promised to title is Dillihani territory, and has sent surveyors.

choices.label: Insist: not one metre
Propose a joint border commission
Blame the government's weakness

country.note: Now claims the Fauran pastures as its own territory.

EVENTS.title: Trueant troops move to the border
EVENTS.text: After your "Greater Cranebonistan" speech, the Southern Trueants have moved two divisions to the Alinni border.

choices.label: Double down
Say you meant the economy
Blame the media for twisting your words

country.note: Moved two divisions to the Alinni border.

EVENTS.title: Golba warns of "consequences"
EVENTS.text: Golba's trade secretary says Cranebonistan's boycott campaign "will not go unanswered". Yamlin's exporters are panicking.

choices.label: Defy Golba
Say it's only about consumer choice
Propose friendly trade talks

EVENTS.title: Bombing in Alinni
EVENTS.text: A group calling itself Free Alinni has bombed a police station in the regional capital. Nine people are dead. The country is in shock.

government.text: The government declares a state of emergency in Alinni.

choices.label: Demand a crackdown and a ban on the APV
Condemn the violence and call for calm
Call for talks with moderate Alinnian leaders

country.note: Accused of arming the Free Alinni separatists.

EVENTS.title: Curfew and mass arrests in Alinni
EVENTS.text: Two thousand Alinnians have been arrested under the emergency laws. Most have not been charged with anything.

government.text: The Interior Minister says the arrests are "saving lives".

choices.label: Back the curfew
Demand that courts review every arrest
Blame the government for letting it happen

EVENTS.title: The Free Alinni commander is caught
EVENTS.text: Police have arrested the man behind the bombing campaign. The trial will be the biggest in Cranebonian history.

choices.label: Demand the harshest possible sentence
Call for a fair trial and a reconciliation commission
Take credit for pushing the government to act

country.note: Denies any link to the captured Free Alinni commander.

EVENTS.title: Bordon tanks cross into James
EVENTS.text: The Bordon Federation has invaded James. The generalissimo says he is "reuniting the family". James begs Cranebonistan for help.

government.text: The government says the army is not ready for war and will send only supplies and ammunition.

choices.label: Demand that troops be sent anyway
Back supplies-only as the wise choice
Blame the government for a hollow army

country.note: Invaded by the Bordon Federation.
Invaded James to "reunite the family".

EVENTS.title: Refugees from James reach Erland
EVENTS.text: James's capital is under siege. Thirty thousand refugees are walking north into Erland's border towns.

choices.label: Open Erland's towns to them
Demand camps at the border
Demand a ban on Bordon grain

country.note: Its capital is under siege. Thousands of refugees are fleeing north into Erland.

EVENTS.title: Ceasefire: James loses its mining valleys
EVENTS.text: A ceasefire has been signed. Bordon keeps the valleys where most of James's rare materials are mined.

choices.label: Call it a national humiliation
Call it the least bad outcome
Demand Cranebonian guards for the remaining mines

country.note: Lost its mining valleys to Bordon in the ceasefire.
Holds James's mining valleys under the ceasefire.

EVENTS.title: Golban banks collapse; the Pezo is in free fall
EVENTS.text: Three of Golba's biggest banks have failed in a week. Cranebonian savings are evaporating and queues are forming outside banks in Cranebo.

government.text: The government closes the banks for three days "to restore calm".

choices.label: Demand capital controls and nationalised banks
Demand spending cuts to calm the markets
Blame foreign speculators

country.note: Its already weak economy has collapsed further in the global crisis.
Weathering the global crisis better than any of its neighbours.

EVENTS.title: Factories close across Cranbia
EVENTS.text: A hundred and twenty thousand jobs have gone in two months. Whole towns in Cranbia's industrial belt have nothing left.

choices.label: Demand the state take over the factories
Demand tax cuts to save businesses
Demand jobs for Cranebonians first

EVENTS.title: Bread riots in Yamlin
EVENTS.text: Food prices have doubled. Crowds looted warehouses in Yamlin overnight, and the army is on the streets.

choices.label: Demand price controls on food
Demand the army restore order
March with the hungry

EVENTS.title: Arson attack on an Alinnian community centre
EVENTS.text: Six people died when a group calling itself the Black Wheat set fire to an Alinnian community centre in Cranbia. Nationalist slogans were painted on the walls.

government.text: The prime minister calls it "a tragedy" but avoids the word terrorism.

choices.label: Condemn it clearly and visit the families
Condemn it, but say the anger is understandable
Suggest foreign provocateurs did it

EVENTS.title: The Black Wheat attacks a Norbanian shelter
EVENTS.text: A shelter for Norbanian refugees in Yamlin was firebombed overnight. Nobody died, but the message is clear.

choices.label: Demand the Black Wheat be declared terrorists
Say there are extremists on both sides
Say nothing

EVENTS.title: Black Wheat leaders arrested
EVENTS.text: Police have arrested the Black Wheat's leaders. Newspapers have found photographs of one of them at your rallies.

choices.label: Apologise and tighten who can join your rallies
Say you never met him
Accuse the police of targeting patriots

EVENTS.title: Troops mass on the Trueant border
EVENTS.text: The government has moved three divisions to the border. The prime minister speaks of "historic lands" south of Alinni. Crowds wave flags in Cranebo.

government.text: The prime minister says Cranebonistan "will not apologise for its history".

choices.label: Join the chorus
Warn against a war nobody can win
Say the government is using war to hide its failures

country.note: Cranebonian divisions are massed on its border.

EVENTS.title: Four soldiers killed in a border clash
EVENTS.text: Four Cranebonian soldiers died in an exchange of fire with Trueant troops. Their funerals are on every channel.

choices.label: Demand retaliation
Demand a ceasefire and talks
Attend the funerals in silence

country.note: Its troops killed four Cranebonian soldiers in a border clash.

EVENTS.title: Golba brokers a deal; the government claims victory
EVENTS.text: Under Golban pressure, both sides have pulled back. The government says Cranebonistan "stood tall". Not a metre of land has changed hands.

choices.label: Say the government won nothing
Welcome the peace
Say next time it should be finished properly

country.note: An uneasy truce with Cranebonistan, brokered by Golba.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱5M from the Yamlin Chamber of Commerce
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Legal and public. Voters will see you as more pro-business.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱3M from the Metalworkers' Union
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Legal and public. Voters will see you as more pro-worker.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱7M in cash from construction tycoon Orvan Sell
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: No paperwork. He will expect favours, and cash has a way of being found.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱12M through a Dillihan state energy company
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Secret foreign money. If it leaks, Fauran and nationalists will never forgive you.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱10M from Southern Trueant intermediaries
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Secret foreign money from the country that claims Alinni. The most dangerous money there is.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱9M from a Potanian mining company
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Secret foreign money. They want influence over the James mining deals.

FUNDING_OFFERS.title: ₱8M in ad spending from a Golban trade lobby
FUNDING_OFFERS.note: Hidden foreign money, but from a friendly country. A leak would hurt less.

INITIATIVES.title: Propose a referendum on autonomy for Alinni
INITIATIVES.text: Let Alinni vote on running its own schools, police and budget.
INITIATIVES.quote: Let the people of Alinni decide how they want to be governed.

INITIATIVES.title: Launch a campaign to deport undocumented Norbanians
INITIATIVES.text: Posters, rallies and a petition calling for mass deportations.
INITIATIVES.quote: If you came here illegally, you will leave legally.

INITIATIVES.title: Propose a one-off tax on the 500 richest families
INITIATIVES.text: A single levy on the country's biggest fortunes, to pay for schools and hospitals.
INITIATIVES.quote: Five hundred families own half of Cranebonistan. They can spare a little of it.

INITIATIVES.title: Call for doubling the defence budget
INITIATIVES.text: A campaign for a stronger army, navy and border guard.
INITIATIVES.quote: A country that cannot defend itself is a country waiting to be divided.

INITIATIVES.title: Meet Trueant opposition leaders in secret
INITIATIVES.text: Quiet talks with the people who may run the Southern Trueants one day.
INITIATIVES.quote: Peace is made with the next government, not the current one.

INITIATIVES.title: Publish a list of corrupt officials
INITIATIVES.text: Name names. Your researchers have a list of thirty officials.
INITIATIVES.quote: Here are the names. Let them sue me.

INITIATIVES.title: Promise to double the state pension
INITIATIVES.text: A simple, enormous promise to every retiree.
INITIATIVES.quote: They built this country. They should not have to choose between heating and eating.

INITIATIVES.title: Call for a defence pact with James
INITIATIVES.text: A formal promise to defend James if it is attacked.
INITIATIVES.quote: James trusted us. A promise to a friend should be written down.

INITIATIVES.title: Launch a "Family and Faith" campaign
INITIATIVES.text: Religion back in schools, tax breaks for married couples, and posters of grandparents.
INITIATIVES.quote: A country that forgets its grandparents' values will not have grandchildren.

INITIATIVES.title: Promise land titles to Fauran's herders
INITIATIVES.text: Legal ownership of the grazing lands the nomads have used for centuries.
INITIATIVES.quote: The land the herds walk on belongs to the people who walk with them.

INITIATIVES.title: Speak of a "Greater Cranebonistan" at a rally
INITIATIVES.text: Hint, in front of a big crowd, that the country's borders are not final.
INITIATIVES.quote: Our grandfathers' maps were bigger than ours. Maybe our grandchildren's will be too.

INITIATIVES.title: Call for a boycott of Golban goods
INITIATIVES.text: "Buy Cranebonian": a national campaign against imports.
INITIATIVES.quote: Every Golban phone you buy pays a Golban salary. Buy Cranebonian.

CRISES.name: Bordon invades James
CRISES.blurb: The Federation attacks James. Cranebonistan can only send supplies.

CRISES.name: The Great Contraction
CRISES.blurb: A global economic crisis reaches Cranebonistan.

CRISES.name: Drums of war
CRISES.blurb: Cranebonistan postures for war with the Southern Trueants.

press.viral: Commentators called it the most serious answer anyone gave.
press.gaffe: Critics called it stiff and evasive.

press.normal: Supporters loved the passion; critics called it shouting.
press.viral: The clip of you saying it is on every channel.
press.gaffe: You lost your temper on camera, and it shows.

press.normal: It came across as down to earth.
press.viral: The line has become a catchphrase.
press.gaffe: The joke fell flat, and people noticed.

press.viral: The most shared clip of the month. Love it or hate it, everyone saw it.
press.gaffe: Even people who agree with you are wincing.

weathervane.title: The Weathervane
weathervane.line: Said whatever the wind was blowing that week, and the wind kept changing.

believer.title: The True Believer
believer.line: Never moved an inch. Whether that was principle or stubbornness, the voters decided.

strongman.title: The Strongman
strongman.line: Loud, certain, and adored by a crowd that would follow anywhere.

clown.title: The Clown Prince
clown.line: Every week a new outrage, and every outrage a few more followers.

technocrat.title: The Technocrat
technocrat.line: Measured, careful, and forgettable to everyone except the middle class.

fixer.title: The Fixer
fixer.line: Knew where the money was, and where the bodies were buried.

demagogue.title: The Demagogue
demagogue.line: Always had someone to blame, and never ran out of people.

champion.label: Champion an issue
champion.help: Campaign hard on one of your manifesto's issues to win its single-issue voters: people who care about that issue above everything else. You can campaign on two issues at a time. Claims are cheapest while nobody is talking about the issue; when it later dominates the news, many more voters become single-issue voters and its owner gains most.

grassroots.label: Grassroots organising
grassroots.help: Door-to-door work and local branches in one region. Turns supporters into core voters and gets them to the polls. Slow, but it lasts.

research.label: Opposition research
research.help: Pay investigators to dig into a rival. You may find something you can release later. You may also get caught.

release.label: Release a dossier
release.help: Leak what you found to the press. It weakens the rival's support and stability, and lowers trust in politics, which helps outsiders like you.

poach.label: Recruit defectors
poach.help: Only possible when a rival is unstable, and once every six months per party. Win over some of their local organisers and core voters, but they bring their views with them.

outrage.label: Provoke outrage
outrage.help: Say something deliberately shocking to get your party's name everywhere. Recognition jumps and anti-system voters cheer, but the middle class is appalled and business donors back away.

SCRUTINY_STORIES.title: Newspaper digs into your party's finances
SCRUTINY_STORIES.text: A long investigation questions where your money comes from. Nothing illegal yet, but the headlines hurt.

SCRUTINY_STORIES.title: Old videos of your leader resurface
SCRUTINY_STORIES.text: Clips of your leader's past speeches are circulating, edited to look as extreme as possible.

SCRUTINY_STORIES.title: Rivals unite against you
SCRUTINY_STORIES.text: The other party leaders appeared together to warn that your party is "a danger to Cranebonistan".

SCRUTINY_STORIES.title: Your candidates' gaffes go viral
SCRUTINY_STORIES.text: A local candidate of yours was filmed saying something unrepeatable. The clip is everywhere.

cranebonistan.name: Cranebonistan
cranebonistan.note: Navy for the northern sea, white for peace, gold for Erland's wheat. The red disc carries the crane that gives the country its name.

trueants.name: Southern Trueants
trueants.note: Orange and black, with the single star of the ruling party.

dillihan.name: Dillihan Republic
dillihan.note: Green for its farmland, the gold star of its republican revolution.

bourdeaux.name: Bordon Federation
bourdeaux.note: One star for each of its five nations, held together by the generalissimo's sabre.

james.name: James
james.note: Slate for its mountains, a gold seam for the rare ores beneath them.

golba.name: United Federation of Golba
golba.note: The biggest power in the world and Cranebonistan's main trading partner.

norbanistan.name: Norbanistan
norbanistan.note: The flag of the old state, still flown by every side in its civil war.

potania.name: Potania
potania.note: The violet and silver of the world's biggest buyer of rare materials.
